finding: The prescribing information describes phosphorylation of acyclovir by viral thymidine kinase followed by inhibition of herpesvirus DNA polymerase.
directness_notes: UL23 is required for efficient prodrug activation; this record does not identify UL23 as the direct inhibitory binding target.
review_notes: Requires pharmacist/virologist verification against the cited label.

finding: The activated acyclovir metabolite inhibits herpesvirus DNA polymerase and terminates viral DNA synthesis.
directness_notes: The label supports the polymerase mechanism; the gene-to-protein mapping to HSV-2 UL30 requires named human review.
review_notes: Requires pharmacist/virologist verification against the cited label.

finding: A randomized clinical study evaluated the helicase-primase inhibitor pritelivir in persons with genital HSV-2 infection.
directness_notes: Clinical activity supports the viral helicase-primase complex as an intervention route but does not alone prove direct binding to UL5.
review_notes: Requires clinical/virology review of the full article.

finding: ChEMBL represents the HSV-2 helicase/primase complex with UL5, UL8, and UL52 protein components.
directness_notes: A complex component record is not evidence that pritelivir directly binds every listed subunit; the current ChEMBL target record has no direct activity row for this complex.
review_notes: Requires pharmacology review of the target record and associated assay evidence.

finding: A clinical resistance analysis examined UL5 and UL52 regions after four weeks of pritelivir exposure and reported no evidence of resistance selection in that study.
directness_notes: Absence of detected resistance in one study is not proof that resistance cannot emerge.
review_notes: Requires virology review of methods, sequencing boundaries, and statistical interpretation.
